subject: Neurology
vignette: A medical student traces the path of cerebrospinal fluid through a brain specimen. CSF is generated within the ventricles and flows sequentially through a series of interconnected cavities before it reaches the subarachnoid space surrounding the brain and spinal cord.
question: Through which structure does cerebrospinal fluid pass from the lateral ventricles into the third ventricle?

options.text: Central canal of the spinal cord

explanation_correct: The paired interventricular foramina of Monro connect each lateral ventricle to the third ventricle, allowing CSF to flow from the lateral ventricles into the third ventricle. From there CSF passes through the cerebral aqueduct of Sylvius into the fourth ventricle before exiting to the subarachnoid space.

explanation_incorrect.A: The cerebral aqueduct of Sylvius connects the third ventricle to the fourth ventricle, not the lateral ventricles to the third.
explanation_incorrect.B: The foramen of Magendie is the medial aperture through which the fourth ventricle drains into the subarachnoid space.
explanation_incorrect.D: The foramina of Luschka are the lateral apertures of the fourth ventricle into the subarachnoid space.
explanation_incorrect.E: The central canal is the narrow CSF-containing channel within the spinal cord, continuous with the fourth ventricle; it is not the route from the lateral to the third ventricle.

educationalObjective: CSF flows from the lateral ventricles to the third ventricle through the interventricular foramina of Monro.

subject: Neurology
vignette: An educational animation shows cerebrospinal fluid leaving the fourth ventricle through three openings to enter the subarachnoid space. One opening is located in the midline, while the other two are situated laterally on either side.
question: Which of the following are the lateral apertures of the fourth ventricle?

options.text: Central canal of the spinal cord

explanation_correct: The fourth ventricle drains into the subarachnoid space through three openings: the paired lateral foramina of Luschka and the single medial foramen of Magendie. These apertures allow CSF produced by the choroid plexuses to leave the ventricular system and circulate around the brain and spinal cord before reabsorption.

explanation_incorrect.B: The foramen of Magendie is the single medial aperture of the fourth ventricle, not the lateral openings.
explanation_incorrect.C: The interventricular foramina of Monro connect the lateral ventricles to the third ventricle and are not exits of the fourth ventricle.
explanation_incorrect.D: The cerebral aqueduct of Sylvius carries CSF from the third to the fourth ventricle; it is an inlet, not an outlet of the fourth ventricle.
explanation_incorrect.E: The central canal is a narrow continuation of the fourth ventricle into the spinal cord, not a lateral aperture.

educationalObjective: The foramina of Luschka are the lateral exits and the foramen of Magendie is the medial exit of the fourth ventricle into the subarachnoid space.

subject: Neurology
vignette: A researcher studies cerebrospinal fluid dynamics. CSF is generated by specialized ependymal structures within the ventricles, circulates through the ventricular system and subarachnoid space, and is then reabsorbed into the venous circulation through clusters of modified arachnoid cells projecting into dural sinuses.
question: Which of the following correctly pairs the site of CSF production with the site of CSF reabsorption?

options.text: Ependymal lining of the central canal; choroid plexus of the lateral ventricle
Arachnoid granulations; choroid plexuses of the third ventricle
Choroid plexus of the fourth ventricle only; foramina of Luschka and Magendie
Choroid plexuses of the lateral, third, and fourth ventricles; arachnoid granulations into dural venous sinuses
Cerebral cortex; direct absorption into the internal jugular vein without dural sinuses

explanation_correct: CSF is produced by choroid plexuses located in the lateral, third, and fourth ventricles. After flowing through the ventricles and exiting via the foramina of Luschka and Magendie into the subarachnoid space, it is reabsorbed by arachnoid granulations that drain into the dural venous sinuses and ultimately into the internal jugular vein.

explanation_incorrect.A: CSF is not produced by the ependymal lining of the central canal, and the choroid plexus is a site of production rather than reabsorption.
explanation_incorrect.B: This reverses the actual arrangement: arachnoid granulations reabsorb CSF, while choroid plexuses produce it.
explanation_incorrect.C: Choroid plexuses are present in the lateral, third, and fourth ventricles, not only the fourth, and the Luschka/Magendie foramina are flow outlets rather than reabsorption sites.
explanation_incorrect.E: The cerebral cortex does not produce CSF, and reabsorption occurs through arachnoid granulations into dural venous sinuses before reaching the internal jugular vein.

educationalObjective: CSF is produced by choroid plexuses in the lateral, third, and fourth ventricles and reabsorbed by arachnoid granulations into dural venous sinuses.

subject: Neurology
vignette: A 4-month-old infant presents with rapidly increasing head circumference, a bulging fontanelle, and downward deviation of the eyes. Imaging shows marked enlargement of the lateral and third ventricles with a normal-sized fourth ventricle and no enlargement of the subarachnoid space over the cerebral convexities.
question: At which level of the CSF pathway is the obstruction in this patient?

options.text: Choroid plexus of the lateral ventricles

explanation_correct: Obstruction of the cerebral aqueduct of Sylvius prevents CSF from passing from the third to the fourth ventricle, so the lateral and third ventricles enlarge proximal to the block while the fourth ventricle remains normal. This produces a noncommunicating (obstructive) hydrocephalus with no dilation of the subarachnoid space, matching the imaging findings.

explanation_incorrect.A: Obstruction of the foramina of Monro would enlarge only the lateral ventricles and would spare the third ventricle, which is dilated in this infant.
explanation_incorrect.C: Obstruction at the outlets of the fourth ventricle would also enlarge the fourth ventricle, rather than leaving it normal-sized.
explanation_incorrect.D: Failure of arachnoid granulation reabsorption causes communicating hydrocephalus with dilated subarachnoid spaces, not isolated ventricular enlargement.
explanation_incorrect.E: The choroid plexus produces CSF; a production abnormality would not create a focal block with a normal fourth ventricle and spared subarachnoid space.

educationalObjective: Aqueductal stenosis causes noncommunicating hydrocephalus with enlarged lateral and third ventricles but a normal fourth ventricle.
